original_description: Use whenever a task involves TanStack Query or @tanstack/react-query in a React or Next.js codebase, especially QueryClient setup, query hook design, query key factories, dependent queries, mutations, optimistic updates, invalidation, hydration, dehydrate/HydrationBoundary, observer-count performance, staleTime/gcTime tuning, or multi-layer caching with Next.js App Router. best_description: Use this skill when the user is trying to decide the right TanStack Query / React Query shape for an app: how server data should be fetched, keyed, cached, hydrated, invalidated, or updated in React or Next.js. Reach for it for setup, reviews, audits, migrations, and debugging when TanStack Query is the main server-state layer: QueryClient defaults, query-key structure, staleTime/gcTime policy, dependent queries, mutations, optimistic updates, stale data, duplicate requests, or refetch churn. It is especially relevant in Next.js App Router when the question is about server/client cache boundaries: prefetching, dehydrate/HydrationBoundary, per-request QueryClient setup, useSuspenseQuery, or keeping server actions and cache tags aligned with client invalidation. Skip it for SWR, plain fetch, Zustand, local UI state, or backend-only caching unless TanStack Query is central.
